Budget Watch
Recall of House approved-GAB may lead to reenacted budget – senators
Oct 23, 2026 6:14 PM PHT
Sundy Locus
Senators and officials of the Department of Agriculture (DA) review the proposed 2027 budget of the DA and its attached agencies and corporations, on October 21, 2026. Under the 2027 National Expenditure Program, the DA is set to receive ₱198.4 billion, an 8 percent decrease from its ₱215.7-billion budget in 2026.
Senate Social Media Unit
INFO
Senators say concerns over the House-approved General Appropriations Bill can be addressed in the consolidated version of the budget bill
AT A GLANCE
Senators warn that recalling the House-approved 2027 national budget could lead to delays and a reenacted budget.
The Makabayan bloc is pushing for the recall to correct potentially unconstitutional provisions, but Senate leaders argue that this is not the solution.
Senate President Gatchalian believes the Senate can address concerns in the consolidated budget bill without needing a recall.
This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context.

.
MANILA, Philippines – Recalling the House-approved version of the 7.2-trillion proposed 2027 national budget, as pushed by some lawmakers, may result in a reenacted budget, senators said on Friday, October 23.
Senate finance committee chairperson
JV Ejercito
warned of potential delays in the passage of the 2027 General Appropriations Bill (GAB) after the Makabayan bloc proposed recalling House Bill No. 10858 to correct provisions they believe could be declared unconstitutional.
“There are proposals to recall the HGAB. In my opinion, there is a great chance the proposed 2027 national budget may not be approved if that would happen,” Ejercito said in a chance interview.
“The Senate is running on a very tight schedule due to the impeachment, regular plenary sessions, and budget hearings. Right now, we are targeting to pass our version of the budget bill by second week of November,” he added
The Supreme Court (SC)
declared
the 2024 and 2025 General Appropriations Acts (GAA), or national budget laws, unconstitutional. Citing the court’s rulings, the Makabayan bloc called on the House to “clean its own mess,” pointing to provisions in the proposed 2027 budget involving the release of unprogrammed appropriations, cuts to foreign-assisted projects to accommodate congressional insertions, and prohibited lump-sum allocations.
ACT Teachers Representative Antonio Tinio told ANC’s
Headstart
: “If this were not corrected, [it] would risk many portions of the budget for 2027 as well. We don’t want yet another budget that will be declared unconstitutional.”
Senator
Panfilo “Ping” Lacson
, chairperson of the Senate committee on accounts, echoed Ejercito’s position, saying recalling the budget was “not the solution.”
“They can submit their proposals to the House or to the Senate finance committee for consideration. After all, the Senate version of the budget bill will be subject to the bicam so they should attest and address their concerns there,” Lacson said.
“Recalling the budget to the House is not the solution because that would result to a worse scenario — a reenacted budget,” he added.
Senate President
Sherwin Gatchalian
also said there was no need to recall the proposed budget, adding that the Senate could address the questioned provisions in the consolidated version of the budget bill.
“Looking at the Supreme Court decision on the 2026 budget, there are only a few provisions that will be affected. I don’t see the need to make major correction in the 2027 budget,” Gatchalian said.
Under the 1987 Constitution, if Congress fails to pass the GAB for the incoming fiscal year, the GAA for the preceding fiscal year is deemed reenacted and remains in effect until a new appropriations law is passed. –
Rappler.com

efet_title: De Lima, Diokno, 8 other House lawmakers want China envoy recalled - Rappler
efet_body:
Philippines-China relations
De Lima, Diokno, 8 other House lawmakers want China envoy recalled
Oct 21, 2026 2:25 PM PHT
Dwight de Leon
LOWER CHAMBER. The House of Representatives Session Hall.
House of Representatives' Facebook page
INFO
The lawmakers say the President must 'take decisive action in response to statements and conduct that undermine national sovereignty and threaten the country's security'
AT A GLANCE
Ten House lawmakers in the Philippines filed House Resolution No. 1562 urging President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to declare Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan persona non grata or request his recall from Beijing.
The resolution was prompted by Jing's controversial statement perceived as a threat to the Philippines, alongside the Chinese Embassy's dismissive response to the lawmakers' concerns.
The lawmakers emphasized the need for decisive action to protect national sovereignty and criticized the Chinese Embassy's language as undiplomatic and arrogant.
This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context.
Report any errors
.
MANILA, Philippines – Ten House lawmakers filed a proposed resolution urging President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to either declare Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan
persona non grata
or ask Beijing to recall him.
House Senior Deputy Minority Leader Leila de Lima (Mamamayang Liberal) and House Assistant Minority Leader Chel Diokno (Akbayan) joined eight other lawmakers in authoring House Resolution No. 1562, filed on Wednesday, October 21.
Play Video
Their move followed
similar resolutions
filed in the upper chamber by senators Erwin Tulfo and Risa Hontiveros.
Other lawmakers who signed the House resolution are:
House Assistant Majority Leader and Lanao del Sur 1st District Representative Zia Adiong
House Assistant Majority Leader and Las Pinas Representative Mark Santos
Zamboanga del Norte 3rd District Representative Adrian Michael Amatong
Pinoy Workers Representative Karl Legazpi
House Deputy Minority Leader and Akbayan Representative Perci Cendana
House Deputy Minority Leader and Dinagat Islands Representative Kaka Bag-ao
House Deputy Minority Leader and Albay 1st District Representative Krisel Lagman
Akbayan Representative Dadah Ismula
“Under the Constitution, the President, being vested with foreign power, holds primary authority to conduct foreign relations and to represent the nation in its dealings with other states, and must therefore take decisive action in response to statements and conduct that undermine national sovereignty and threaten the country’s security,” the proposed resolution read.
The lawmakers cite a number of incidents that led to the filing of the resolution, starting with Jing’s October 15 statement saying that if China wants to use force, “we may easily win.” Philippine government officials, including the President, later said the statement sounded like a threat.
The Chinese Embassy dared the Senate and the House to just declare Jing as persona non grata and “stop bluffing.” It also threatened to block Philippine officials from entering China if Jing were to be declared persona non grata.
Before the group of House lawmakers filed the resolution, they sounded the alarm over Jing’s seeming threat against the Philippines, and the Chinese embassy’s subsequent language that seemed dismissive of Filipinos’ sentiments.
“The embassy’s undiplomatic language taunting our government to declare the Chinese ambassador as persona non grata does little to encourage serious dialogue between two sovereign nations. Instead it reflects their position that our country should simply accept China’s threats and submit to its demands,” they said.
“The Philippines must not be cowed into silence in the face of such arrogance,” the lawmakers added.
– Rappler.com

efet_body:
Filtered By: Topstories
News
By LYJAH TIFFANY BONZO, GMA News
Published
October 25, 2026 8:25pm
+
Add GMA on Google
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.
Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan's remarks are unacceptable, the fishers groups said.
Fisherfolk in Palawan supported on Sunday
calls by lawmakers to request the recall
of Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan following his statement that Beijing could “easily win” if it resorts to force against the Philippines.
In a press conference of the Atin Ito Coalition in Palawan, leaders of fisherfolk groups also condemned China’s continued aggression toward their livelihood in the West Philippine Sea (WPS).
“Hindi katanggap-tanggap ang pagbabanta ng kinatawan ng isang dayuhang bansa sa Pilipinas. Sinusuportahan namin ang panawagang pauwiin na sa China si Jing Quan,” said Rafaela David, an Atin Ito co-convenor and the Akbayan Party president.
(Threats from a representative of a foreign nation against the Philippines are unacceptable. We support the call to send Jing Quan back to China.)
Other Stories
House members urge Marcos to seek Chinese envoy Jing Quan's recall
China towing away BRP Sierra Madre is 'act of war' against PH — Teodoro
China weaponizing commodities, people amid territorial row, says Teodoro
“Hindi dapat bigyan ng puwang sa ating bansa ang mga katulad niya na nagbabanta sa ating bayan habang inaagawan ng kabuhayan ang ating mga mangingisda,” she added.
(Individuals like him who threaten our nation while robbing our fisherfolk of their livelihood should have no place in our country.)
The group emphasized that China’s actions in the WPS threaten their safety at sea, as well as their families’ livelihoods and food security.
It added that “every fishing trip disrupted by Chinese harassment means lost income and food off the table for families who depend on the sea.”
Atin Ito said the calls to expel Jing were backed by leaders of the Samahan ng mga Mangingisda kontra Korapsyon (SAMAKKO), Samahan ng mga Katutubo at Maliit na Mangingisda sa Dulong Timog Palawan (SAMBIL OG), Kalayaan, Palawan Farmers and Fisherfolk Association, Tinig ng mga Katutubo (TIKA), and Samahang Pagkakaisa ng mga Katutubong Tagbanua sa Marufinas.
Demands to expel the Chinese envoy grew following his remarks that Beijing could “easily win” should it use force against the Philippines, but it chose peace instead.
Senator Risa Hontiveros already
filed a resolution
calling on President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. to declare Jing Quan persona non grata or request his recall by the Chinese government.
Malacañang had earlier said that it would leave the matter to the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA), noting that Marcos does not favor declaring any foreign envoy persona non grata.
The DFA formally summoned Jing Quan on Monday to convey the Philippines' "serious concern and strong objection" to his recent remarks.
— BM, GMA News

efet_body:

By
LLANESCA T. PANTI
, GMA News
Published
October 21, 2026 8:56pm
+

Ten members of the House of Representatives called on President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos, Jr. to declare Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan persona non grata, or ask China to recall him, over his reference to using force in relation to the Philippines.
Lawmakers led by House Senior Deputy Minority Leader Leila de Lima made the call under House Resolution 1562, saying it is in line with the Philippines’ position which renounces war as an instrument of national policy, adopts the generally accepted principles of international law as part of the law of the land and adheres to the policy of peace, equality, justice, freedom, cooperation, and amity with all nations.
“On October 15, 2026, when asked about Secretary of National Defense Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.'s characterization of China as a regional 'troublemaker,' Ambassador Jing Quan, speaking before reporters at the Diliman Dialogues in Quezon City, declared, 'If we want to use force, we may easily win. But no, we will not use force,' further remarking that the Philippines should consider itself fortunate to have China as a neighbor because Beijing would not resort to force because it loved peace,” the Resolution read.
“Under the Constitution, the President, being vested with executive power, holds primary authority to conduct foreign relations and to represent the nation in its dealings with other states and must, therefore, take decisive action in response to statements and conduct that undermine national sovereignty and threaten the country's security,” the Resolution added.
Other Stories
Palawan fishers support calls to request recall of Chinese envoy
China towing away BRP Sierra Madre is 'act of war' against PH — Teodoro
China weaponizing commodities, people amid territorial row, says Teodoro
In addition, the lawmakers cited that the Chinese Embassy in Manila addressed the members of the Senate and the House of Representatives who proposed declaring Ambassador Jing persona non grata for the aforementioned statements, daring the members of the Philippine Congress to "Just do it” and accused Filipino reporters and politicians of "exaggeration, taking things out of context, and creating hype.”
“These incidents demonstrate China's disregard for the sovereign rights of the Philippines and underscore the inconsistency between the Chinese Government's words and its actions. Now, therefore, be it resolved, that the House of Representatives urge the President of the Philippines to declare Ambassador Jing Quan of the People's Republic of China persona non grata, or, in the alternative, to request his recall by the Government of the People's Republic of China,” the Resolution said.
Other co-authors of the Resolution include:
Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong, Lanao del Sur 1st District
Adrian Michael A. Amatong, Zamboanga del Norte 3rd District
Kaka Bag-ao, Dinagat Islands
Percival V. Cendaña, Akbayan Partylist
Leila M. De Lima, ML Partylist
Jose Manuel Tadeo “Chel” I. Diokno, Akbayan Partylist
Dadah Kiram Ismula, Akbayan Partylist
Cielo Krisel Lagman, Albay 1st District
Karl Fernandez Legazpi, PINOY WORKERS Partylist
Mark Anthony G. Santos, Las Piñas
— BM, GMA News
